promptSummary: Bakery: Dos Rios Panaderia, Chicago IL (dos-rios-panaderia.example). Does this bakery already take online orders? Find: how customers place an order today, how many locations it runs, and who owns or manages it. Cite the page you took each fact from.
teachingNote: Five turns, one more than the other three bakeries: search, read three pages at once, one narrow follow-up search, read the outside listing that search found, then stop and write. Nobody wrote that extra step down in advance - the model chose it because the narrow search returned a page it had not seen. Then it did the harder thing: it wrote NOT FOUND instead of turning a stale listing into a fact.

modelTurns.assistantText: I do not know which pages exist yet, so I will search for the bakery first and pick the pages worth reading from the results.

toolArguments.searchQueryText: Dos Rios Panaderia Chicago IL online orders locations owner

modelTurns.assistantText: The search returned three of the bakery's own pages: home, menu and about. There is no order page in the results. I will read all three, in one batch, rather than one at a time.

Locations and owner are settled: one shop, owned by Elena Villarreal. How orders are taken is not. The menu prices whole cakes and party trays, but none of the three pages says how a customer orders one. A bakery can be listed on an outside ordering or delivery service without saying so on its own site, so I will run one more search aimed only at delivery and online ordering.

toolArguments.searchQueryText: Dos Rios Panaderia Chicago delivery order online

modelTurns.assistantText: The narrow search returned one page I have not read: a delivery-directory listing on somebody else's site whose snippet says "order delivery." A snippet is not evidence. I will read the page behind it before I decide what it proves.

RESEARCH REPORT — Dos Rios Panaderia, Chicago IL (dos-rios-panaderia.example)

HOW ORDERS ARE TAKEN: NOT FOUND. The bakery's own pages never say how orders are taken. The home page gives hours, one address, a phone number (312-555-0123) and photos, with no order button, no cart and no link to an ordering service. The menu page lists whole cakes (for example "Tres leches | quarter sheet, serves 20 to 25 | $58") and party trays with prices, and says "Writing on the cake is included," but it has no order button and no note about ordering by phone, by email, in person or on a form. The about page is silent on ordering too. No page says the bakery takes online orders, and no page says it does not. A narrow search turned up one outside page, a delivery-directory listing whose search snippet says "View the menu and order delivery." The page behind it says "This store is not currently accepting orders." That listing carries no date, says it "was created automatically from public business information" and "has not been claimed by the business," and shows a concha at $1.25 where the bakery's own menu says $1.75, so it is stale. It does not prove the bakery takes delivery orders through a platform, and it does not prove the bakery takes orders by phone or in person.
Source: https://dos-rios-panaderia.example/, https://dos-rios-panaderia.example/menu, https://dos-rios-panaderia.example/about and https://chicago-delivery-directory.example/stores/dos-rios-panaderia

LOCATIONS: One. The about page says "We have one shop. It is the same one we opened in 2009, at 32 Example Street in South Shore, and it is the only place our bread is baked or sold." The home page gives the same single address, 32 Example Street, Chicago, IL 60649, and says "Dos Rios has been in the same spot, under the same family, since 2009."
Source: https://dos-rios-panaderia.example/about and https://dos-rios-panaderia.example/

OWNER OR MANAGER: Elena Villarreal, owner and head baker. The about page says "Dos Rios Panaderia is owned by Elena Villarreal," and that she opened it in 2009. It is family-run: her husband Rodrigo Villarreal maintains the ovens and her daughter Marisol Villarreal runs the front of the shop. The about page gives the address elena@dos-rios-panaderia.example for neighborhood requests.
Source: https://dos-rios-panaderia.example/about

CONFIDENCE: High for locations and owner, which the bakery states directly. Low for how orders are taken: I read all three of the bakery's own pages and the one outside listing, and none of them settles it. More searching is unlikely to help. A person should look at this one, for example by phoning the shop.
